2026-07-29.headline: Note: 29 Jul figures are intraday prints; 28 Jul is now a final close ($82.08 Brent, down $3.79 from 27 Jul's $85.87 — the third consecutive daily decline and, cumulatively, $12.18 off the 23 Jul $94.26 peak close). Restated continuation series (front-month CO2/CL2) in force. Score HOLDS at 25/30 — all six channels unchanged, an eleventh session at 25 — but beneath the flat number the two most consequential things in this edition move in opposite directions. First, the de-escalation survived its biggest scheduled test: the US strike pause held a fourth consecutive night (25–28 Jul), the longest of the war, and the Netanyahu–Trump White House meeting produced no resumption signal — an Israeli official called it an 'excellent and comprehensive discussion... first and foremost Iran' with an 'ironclad' nuclear commitment, and the White House framed both of Tuesday's leader meetings as 'positive and productive.' Oman went further, tabling a Malacca-model joint-management framework with voluntary vessel fees. Second, Iran hardened its terms in the same 24 hours: the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters declared on 28 Jul that vessels of any country or company accepting compensation from Iran's frozen assets 'will not be allowed' to transit, and Tehran separately tabled a rival temporary plan giving itself greater control of the transit lanes. Crude read the second story: after the 28 Jul close, Brent has bounced to $85.04 intraday (H 85.45 / L 83.95, +$2.96), with the active COA contract back to $87.61 from Tuesday's $84.09 close. The reconciliation gap was the widest of the war on the downside — my 28 Jul quote of $85.40 closed $3.32 lower — the third straight session in which the US leg took the tape below the Asia snapshot, a first. On rates the news is a genuine change of state: for the first time in the war both legs of the Treasury channel's downgrade test moved toward release in the same session. The 30Y closed 5.0886%, cutting its cushion above the 5.00% line from 13.65 bp to 8.86 bp (a third consecutive session toward it), and MOVE's confirmed close fell 1.12 to 76.09 — now just 1.09 pts above the 75 leg, the closest of the war. Neither has cleared, so nothing moved; but Treasury 5→4 is now the score's most probable next step, and it is a downgrade. Stage-4 Threshold B disarmed further: the 10Y's 4.6062% close was a second consecutive print below 4.65%, formally resetting that leg's sustained status, and the 30Y sits 11.14 bp below 5.20%. The gasoline blackout partly cleared and the news is a stall, not a break — AAA's backfilled 27 Jul print came in at $4.75, flat, ending the nine-session run of rises exactly ON the political → 5 line without going through it, while the overdue DOE weekly landed at $4.096 (+9.5¢). The inflation leg edged the wrong way again — 5Y5Y closed 2.2667%, 3.33 bp from the trigger. No trigger fired on a confirmed close, so no channel moved; with both event channels maxed, the hold remains an artifact of the scale. The FOMC decides at 2pm ET today with hike odds near a third (roughly 32–38%, against 10.7% on 15 Jul) and Chair Warsh's presser at 2:30 — the single event most likely to resolve the Treasury channel in either direction. Sequencing 25 → 25 → 25.

analysis.intro: The US economic shock holds at 25/30 for an eleventh session, but the composition of the standstill changed materially. On the geopolitical side the de-escalation cleared its highest hurdle: the strike pause reached a fourth night, and the Netanyahu visit — the single most plausible reset event on the calendar — came and went without a resumption signal, while Oman put an actual joint-management framework on the table. On the Iranian side the terms hardened in the same 24 hours, with the Khatam al-Anbiya command threatening transit denial over the frozen-asset compensation scheme and Tehran countering Oman's draft with a plan that concentrates control in its own hands. Crude priced the second story, bouncing $2.96 off a 28 Jul close that had itself fallen $3.79. The more important development is on rates. Until this session the Treasury channel's two downgrade legs had been moving apart — the 30Y toward release, MOVE away from it. On the 28 Jul close they moved together for the first time: the 30Y cut its cushion above 5.00% to 8.86 bp and MOVE fell to 76.09, 1.09 pts from its own line. Neither cleared and neither has sustained, so the channel held at 5 — but a 5→4 downgrade is now the most probable next move in the score, and the FOMC decision at 2pm ET today, with hike odds near a third and a new Chair holding only his second meeting, is the event most likely to settle it in one direction or the other.

bondYield.title: (i) Treasury — held at 5; for the first time in the war both downgrade legs moved toward release together.
bondYield.text: The 30Y closed 28 Jul at 5.0886% — 8.86 bp above the 5.00% downgrade leg, narrowed from 13.65 bp on Monday and 15.74 bp on 24 Jul — a third consecutive session toward its own release line; it prints 5.0969% this morning (9.69 bp) as the curve backs up marginally into the FOMC. MOVE, which had ticked the wrong way on 27 Jul, reversed: the confirmed 28 Jul close fell 1.12 to 76.09, leaving it 1.09 pts above the 75 leg — the closest approach of the war. Both legs must clear simultaneously and sustain to downgrade, so nothing has moved; but the arithmetic is now within a single strong session on each. The FOMC is the binary: hike odds have risen to roughly 32–38% from 10.7% on 15 Jul, and Warsh's framing — 'no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation,' 'prices are too high' — cuts against a dovish surprise, though June payrolls of 57k against 115k expected complicate the case for acting now. A hawkish outcome re-arms the long end from below; a dovish or neutral one puts Treasury 5→4 genuinely in play within the week.

bondYield.title: (ii) Inflation anchor — held at 4; the approach resumed, marginally.
bondYield.text: 5Y5Y closed 28 Jul at 2.2667%, up 0.5 bp from Monday's 2.2617% and now 3.33 bp from the 2.30% line on a close basis, with the intraday at 2.2627% (3.73 bp). That is a second-order move against Friday's 1.2 bp approach, but the direction turned back toward the trigger while crude was falling — a divergence worth watching, since it points at the FOMC and the pass-through story rather than at spot energy. The corroboration is unchanged: the 10Y breakeven closed 2.1955%, below its pre-war anchor for a third consecutive session, consistent with the curve pricing medium-term persistence rather than a near-term spike, and AAA gasoline's backfilled print stalled rather than accelerated. One close above 2.30% starts the clock; a second consecutive close confirms and takes the channel to 5/5 and the score to 26. The downgrade (sustained at or below the 2.142% anchor, 12.1 bp away) is not in play.

bondYield.title: (iii) Oil — held at 2; the close-basis gap to $95 widened to $12.92 before this morning's bounce narrowed it to $9.96.
bondYield.text: Three consecutive daily declines took Brent from the 23 Jul $94.26 peak close to $82.08, a $12.18 unwind, and the active COA contract from $100.69 to $84.09. The 29 Jul intraday reverses part of that — $85.04, up $2.96, with COA at $87.61 — on Iran's frozen-asset transit threat and its rival Hormuz plan, which together reintroduce the risk that the Oman framework stalls on terms rather than on violence. The two-close rule held the channel at 2 through the entire $95 approach and now spares it a symmetric whipsaw on the way down and back up: a downgrade to 1 still needs a mediated pause AND a close at or below the $72.48 anchor, $9.60 away on the 28 Jul close. That is the closest the downgrade has been since early July, and if the Oman framework is signed it becomes the live question rather than the upgrade. (OPEC+'s modest August quota increase and the CPC Black Sea drone-strike risk remain the supply-side crosscurrents; Yanbu loadings are still running ~40% below their pre-19 Jul rate.)

analysis.crossAsset: The unwind ran a third session and then stopped. Crude, European gas and Asia LNG all fell again into the 28 Jul close (Brent $82.08, TTF €57.74, JGLA ¥3,418) and all three bounced this morning or held — Brent +$2.96, TTF +€1.37 — on Iran's transit threat rather than on any change in the strike picture. The Treasury curve rallied through the close and gave a little back intraday, the dollar was flat for a second session at 101.38, and MOVE finally followed spot risk lower after two sessions of refusing to. That last point is the meaningful one: rates vol and spot risk are repricing together again, which is what makes the Treasury channel's two-leg downgrade a live proposition instead of a theoretical one. US Henry Hub is now 13.5% BELOW pre-war, its widest discount of the war — the Hormuz/LNG-routing signature, not a global-energy shock, in its clearest form yet. The political channel's data fog partly lifted: both gasoline series backfilled their 27 Jul prints, and both said the same thing — pass-through continuing (DOE +9.5¢ on the week) but the daily pump series stalling exactly at the trigger.

Hysteresis note: upgrades fire on a sustained break; downgrades only on a sustained reversal past a wider threshold — deliberately, to avoid whipsawing. 2026-07-30.headline: Note: 30 Jul figures are intraday prints. A data flag first: the extract's 29 Jul row did not refresh — every field is identical to my 29 Jul AM snapshot to four decimal places and MOVE, VIX and SOFR are blank, so 29 Jul is a stale snapshot, not a close. The last fully confirmed close is 28 Jul, and all trigger tests below run off it. Score HOLDS at 25/30 — all six channels unchanged, a twelfth session at 25 — and this is the sharpest demonstration of the scale cap the monitor has produced. In twenty-four hours the war's de-escalation track was dismantled and the score did not move. The strike pause is over: after an IRGC ballistic-missile salvo at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base at Azraq in Jordan and a CENTCOM facility — five missiles, all intercepted, no casualties — the US and Saudi Arabia struck Iran-backed militias across eastern Iraq, Riyadh's first offensive combat action of the war, and CENTCOM then resumed strikes on Iranian territory on the night of 29–30 Jul, calling them 'a powerful response to yesterday's attempted Iranian attacks on US forces based in the Middle East.' Trump: 'They're going to get a beating.' The quiet-night count is back to zero after four. Diplomacy went backwards in the same window: Deputy FM Gharibabadi rejected Oman's 50-50 joint-management plan outright on 29 Jul, disavowed the internationally established Traffic Separation Scheme, demanded the entire inbound lane under Iranian control and said the strait 'will remain closed, and we are prepared for a restart of war.' Neither event can raise the score, because maritime and escalation have both been pinned at 5/5 since 10 and 9 Jul. The hold is an artifact of the scale, not a judgment that anything is stable. What the four market channels did is the substantive story, and it is a rates story. The FOMC held at 3.50–3.75% on a 9–3 vote — Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all dissenting for a 25 bp hike — and Chair Warsh, who has removed forward guidance from the statement, insisted 'There is only a target, and it is 2 percent.' The long end did not believe him. The 30Y prints 5.2060%, the first reading above 5.20% in the entire series, up 10.91 bp; the 10Y is 4.6794%, 2.94 bp back above its own 4.65% line; 2s10s has steepened 8.97 bp to +40.67 bp, the largest one-day steepening of the war; the 10Y breakeven is back above its pre-war anchor after three sessions below; and 5Y5Y forward inflation prints 2.3311% — a war high, 3.11 bp through the 2.30% upgrade trigger and only the second reading above 2.30% on record. A hold against three hike dissents, met by a bear steepener with breakevens up and the dollar down 0.51 to 100.87 on a night the US resumed bombing Iran, is the market marking down the Fed's inflation credibility rather than seeking a haven. Two lines that were disarmed yesterday are armed this morning: Stage-4 Threshold B now satisfies both legs simultaneously for the first time in the war, and US-inflation is through its trigger. Neither has a confirmed close behind it, and the two-close rule is the only thing holding the score at 25 — while yesterday's most probable next move, a Treasury 5→4 downgrade, is dead, its cushion above the 5.00% line blown out from 8.86 bp to 20.60 bp. Crude followed the news up but not far: Brent $87.72, +$2.68, still $7.28 below the $95 trigger, active COA $89.96. September hike odds have jumped to roughly 56% from 32–38%. Sequencing 25 → 25 → 25.

Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi rejected Oman’s 50-50 joint-management proposal on state television: ‘If the route we have proposed is not accepted, no other formula will be accepted. The strait will remain closed, and we are prepared for a restart of war.’ Iran also disavowed the internationally established Traffic Separation Scheme and demands the inbound lane entirely under its own control, reportedly at ~$1m per ship against Malacca’s ~$70m a year in voluntary contributions. Oman is weighing a three-route alternative. No US response to the rejection itself could be found. The 28 Jul Khatam al-Anbiya bar on vessels accepting frozen-asset compensation remains in force, and the IRGC Navy said on 29 Jul it ‘targeted and stopped’ three unnamed oil tankers (Tier 3, unconfirmed).

Jizan refinery (400k b/d) still shut since 25 Jul; Yanbu loadings ~3.09 mb/d against ~5.16 before 19 Jul; satellite imagery suggested possible damage at Abqaiq on 27–28 Jul (unverified). Separately, drones struck two gas carriers at Egypt’s Mediterranean port of Damietta on 29 Jul — Gaslog Salem and Energos Winter (US-owned and operated) — fires on both, no casualties, attribution unconfirmed. First strike of the war on that end of the LNG chain.

analysis.intro: The US economic shock holds at 25/30 for a twelfth session while the ground under it moved more than on any day since the crisis-band crossing on 9 Jul. On the event side everything got worse: the strike pause ended, Iran fired at a US base in Jordan, Saudi Arabia joined offensive operations, CENTCOM went back into Iranian territory, and Tehran killed the only mediation framework on the table while saying it is 'prepared for a restart of war.' None of that can move the score, because maritime and escalation have been at 5/5 since 10 and 9 Jul. Readers should take the flat number as evidence that the scale has run out of room on the geopolitical side, not as evidence of stability. The four market channels are where the information is, and this morning they all point the same way for the first time in a fortnight. The FOMC held at 3.50–3.75% against three dissents for a hike, and the long end responded by repricing inflation risk rather than growth risk: the 30Y through 5.20% for the first time on record, 2s10s 9 bp steeper, the 10Y breakeven back above its pre-war anchor, 5Y5Y at a war high through its own trigger, and the dollar lower on a night of renewed strikes. Yesterday's likeliest next move was a Treasury downgrade; today the two live candidates are both upgrades, and both are one confirmed close away.
analysis.bondYieldNote: 30 Jul yields are intraday; the 29 Jul row in the extract is a stale snapshot, so the last confirmed close is 28 Jul and all trigger tests below run off it. No channel moved; score held at 25.

bondYield.title: (i) US inflation impulse — held at 4, but the trigger is through on the print.
bondYield.text: 5Y5Y forward inflation prints 2.3311% this morning: a war high, 3.11 bp above the 2.30% upgrade line, and only the second reading above 2.30% in the whole series after 2.3007% on 7 May. It is up 6.84 bp on the day and 13.16 bp on the week from 2.1995% on 23 Jul. The corroboration turned with it: the 10Y breakeven rose 7.52 bp to 2.2708%, back above its 2.2569% pre-war anchor after three consecutive closes below, so the two measures are no longer telling different stories. The mechanism is legible — a hold against three hike dissents, delivered by a Chair who has removed forward guidance and whose message is rhetorical rather than operational ('There is only a target, and it is 2 percent'; 'where necessary and appropriate, we will not hesitate to act'), against a statement that itself concedes inflation is above target 'due in part to the situation in the Middle East causing energy prices to rise.' The market read that as tolerance and demanded compensation. The discipline is unchanged and it is the whole reason the score is still 25: this is one intraday print, and the channel needs one confirmed close above 2.30% to start the clock and a second consecutive close to fire. On 14 Jul the monitor held this same channel at 3 on a 2.2061% close with a 0.6 bp margin and was vindicated; the same rule now costs a point in the other direction, which is the price of not whipsawing. If it confirms, the channel goes to 5/5 and the score to 26. The downgrade (sustained at or below the 2.142% anchor, now 18.91 bp away) is not in play.

bondYield.title: (ii) Treasury — held at 5; the downgrade that was one session away on Tuesday is now gone.
bondYield.text: The 30Y prints 5.2060%, up 10.91 bp, which widens its cushion above the 5.00% downgrade leg from 8.86 bp on the 28 Jul close to 20.60 bp — a full reversal of three consecutive sessions of approach. The MOVE leg cannot be tested at all: the series has not printed since 28 Jul (76.09), so there is no post-FOMC reading, and with the 30Y up 10.9 bp and the curve 9 bp steeper the honest treatment is that rates vol is unresolved rather than 1.09 pts from release. Both legs must clear simultaneously and sustain; neither is close now. The more important point is the character of the move. This is a bear steepener with breakevens up and the dollar down — 2Y lower 2.5 bp, 30Y higher 10.9 bp, 2s10s +8.97 bp to +40.67 bp, the largest one-day steepening of the war and a 16.4 bp retracement from the 24 Jun low of +24.25 bp. Long-duration risk premium is being rebuilt at the same time as the front end prices less near-term tightening, which is the signature of a market pricing inflation persistence rather than Fed resolve. September hike odds have moved to roughly 56% from 32–38% before the meeting. A Treasury upgrade is not available (the channel is already maxed), so this repricing shows up in the score only through Stage-4 Threshold B and through the inflation channel — which is precisely where it has gone.

bondYield.title: (iii) Oil — held at 2; the news is far worse and the price is only $2.68 better.
bondYield.text: Brent prints $87.72 intraday, a second consecutive gain, with active COA at $89.96 against Tuesday's $84.09 close. But the close-basis gap to the $95 trigger is still $12.92 measured from the last confirmed close, and $7.28 from this morning's print. That is the striking thing about this edition: the pause broke, Saudi Arabia entered the war, mediation collapsed and Iran threatened a restart, and crude added under $3. The physical picture argues for more — Jizan's 400k b/d refinery shut since 25 Jul, Yanbu loadings at ~3.09 mb/d against ~5.16 before 19 Jul, possible Abqaiq damage on 27–28 Jul, roughly 1.5 mb/d of CPC Black Sea exports still at risk, a US crude draw of 7.2 mb to 404.5 mb and refineries at 97.2% of capacity. Against it sit OPEC+ (a fifth consecutive monthly increase of 188k b/d for August, a further ~188k b/d expected at the 2 Aug meeting before a pause after September) and the IEA's remaining stock capacity (290 mb released since 11 March, over 1 bn bbl left). The two-close rule kept this channel at 2 through the $95 approach on 23 Jul and through the $12.18 unwind that followed; it stays at 2 now. The downgrade to 1 needs a mediated pause AND a close at or below $72.48 — and with Oman's framework rejected, the mediated-pause condition has moved from plausible to remote, which effectively takes the downgrade off the table even though the price leg is only $9.60 away.

bondYield.title: (iv) Political — held at 4; the pump series has stalled exactly on its line and the cross-read says it is real.
bondYield.text: AUTMUSAG has not printed since 27 Jul ($4.75), a third consecutive blank session, and per the discipline established after the JGLA episode a missing print is flagged, never carried. The useful new information is external: AAA's own published regular-grade national average went $4.099 on 28 Jul to $4.091 on 29 Jul, the first decline of the run. So the nine-session climb that ended flat exactly at $4.75 on 24–27 Jul looks like a genuine stall rather than a reporting artifact, and the channel is more likely to be held at 4 by the pump than taken to 5 by it. The DOE weekly cuts the other way (+9.5¢ to $4.096 for the week of 27 Jul), and with refineries maxed at 97.2%, gasoline stocks ~6% below the five-year average and the SPR down to ~311 mb from 415 mb in late March, a sustained crude leg higher would pass through quickly. No federal intervention — SPR release, export limit, waiver or gouging action — is confirmable in the 28–30 Jul window.

analysis.stage4Note: Stage 4 is a credit/auction event. Threshold B, disarmed on both legs yesterday, satisfies both legs on this morning’s print for the first time in the war — on an intraday basis only.

stage4.title: Threshold A · 13 May 30Y auction, cleared 5.050%.
stage4.text: Historical benchmark. The 9 Jul re-opening cleared 5.06% with a 0.3 bp stop-through. The 30Y now prints 5.2060%, 15.6 bp above the May stop and the widest margin since that auction. There is no coupon supply until the August refunding cycle, which means the next real test of long-end demand arrives with a curve that has just repriced 11 bp in a session.

stage4.title: Threshold B · 30Y above 5.20% with 10Y above 4.65% — BOTH LEGS ARMED, intraday.
stage4.text: The 30Y prints 5.2060%, 0.60 bp through its leg and the first reading above 5.20% in the series; the 10Y prints 4.6794%, 2.94 bp through its own leg, undoing the reset that two consecutive sub-4.65% closes had produced on 28–29 Jul. This is the first time in the war both legs have been satisfied simultaneously. It is not a Stage-4 event: the threshold is evaluated on confirmed closes and then on persistence, and one Singapore-morning print supplies neither. What it does mean is that B has gone from disarmed to live inside twenty-four hours, and that the mechanism now arming it is domestic monetary credibility rather than a Hormuz headline. A confirmed close on both legs tonight is the single most consequential thing that could happen to this monitor this week.

analysis.crossAsset: The cross-asset signature changed shape. For most of July the tape traded Hormuz headlines: crude, European gas and Asia LNG moved together, the dollar was inert and rates followed risk. This morning the driver is the Fed. Crude and TTF are up (Brent +$2.68, TTF +€1.53, back within €2.95 of the 24 Jul record) on the strike resumption and the collapse of the Omani framework, but the scale of those gains is modest against the scale of the news. The rates complex, by contrast, moved hard and in the specific pattern that says inflation rather than fear: 30Y +10.9 bp, 2s10s +9.0 bp, 10Y breakeven +7.5 bp back through its pre-war anchor, 5Y5Y +6.8 bp to a war high, 2Y –2.5 bp, and DXY –0.51 to 100.87 on a night when the United States resumed bombing Iran. A weaker dollar and steeper curve into renewed war is not a haven bid; it is the market charging a higher premium to hold long-dated US nominal risk. Two gaps qualify the read: MOVE and VIX have no post-FOMC print, so the volatility leg of the story is unmeasured, and equities fell into the 29 Jul close (Dow –1.4%, S&P 500 –0.5%, Nasdaq –0.5%) which the stale VIX does not reflect. Henry Hub remains 10.9% BELOW pre-war — the Hormuz/LNG-routing signature intact, this is still not a global-energy shock — while the Damietta strike on two gas carriers, one US-owned, extends the LNG-chain risk to the Mediterranean for the first time.

channels.name: Maritime denial
channels.rationale: Held at 5 (max). Strait closed to commercial traffic, day ~152; 28 Jul saw 24 AIS-tracked transits plus 15 dark crossings against ~88/day normal, roughly 11% of pre-crisis throughput; ~70% of tanker transits run AIS-off; 371 vessels at anchor; ~80 Iranian mines still in place with third-party clearance refused. Iran rejected the only reopening framework on the table and said the strait ‘will remain closed’; IRGC stopped three more tankers.
channels.downgrade: verified reopening (escorted convoys) with traffic above 25% of normal for 10 sessions → to 3–4.

channels.name: Oil price shock
channels.rationale: Held at 2. Last confirmed close $82.08 (28 Jul), $12.92 below the $95 trigger; intraday $87.72 (+$2.68), $7.28 below it, active COA $89.96. Crude added under $3 on a day that brought a strike resumption, Saudi entry into combat and the collapse of mediation — the supply-side crosscurrents (OPEC+ increases, over 1 bn bbl of IEA stock capacity) are doing real work against the physical damage.
channels.downgrade: mediated pause + close at/below the $72.48 anchor → to 1 (the pause condition is now remote after Iran’s rejection).

channels.name: US inflation impulse
channels.rationale: Held at 4 — but the trigger is THROUGH on this morning’s print. 5Y5Y 2.3311%, a war high, 3.11 bp above the 2.30% line, +6.8 bp d/d and +13.2 bp w/w; only the second reading above 2.30% on record. 10Y breakeven +7.5 bp to 2.2708%, back above its pre-war anchor after three closes below. Needs one confirmed close to start the clock and a second to fire — the two-close rule is the only thing holding this at 4.
channels.downgrade: 5Y5Y sustained at/below the 2.142% pre-war anchor → to 3.

channels.name: Treasury stress
channels.rationale: Held at 5 (max) — and the downgrade that was one session away on Tuesday has gone. The 30Y prints 5.2060%, widening its cushion above the 5.00% leg from 8.86 bp to 20.60 bp; MOVE has not printed since 28 Jul so its 75 leg is unresolved, not cleared. A bear steepener with breakevens up and the dollar down is the FOMC hold being marked as inflation tolerance.
channels.downgrade: 30Y close under 5.00% with MOVE under 75 sustained → to 4.

channels.name: Political stress
channels.rationale: Held at 4. AUTMUSAG has not printed since $4.75 on 27 Jul — a third blank session, flagged and not carried. The external cross-read points to a stall rather than a break: AAA’s published regular-grade average eased from $4.099 (28 Jul) to $4.091 (29 Jul), the first decline of the run. DOE weekly $4.096 (+9.5¢) cuts the other way, and with refineries at 97.2% and the SPR at ~311 mb there is no slack if crude runs.

channels.name: Escalation risk
channels.rationale: Held at 5 (max) on a day that would otherwise have forced an upgrade. The pause is over: an IRGC missile salvo at a US base in Jordan (intercepted), joint US–Saudi strikes on Iran-backed militias in Iraq with at least 20 killed, CENTCOM back over Iranian territory on the night of 29–30 Jul, Iran’s rejection of the Omani plan and its statement that it is ‘prepared for a restart of war,’ plus a first strike on gas carriers at Damietta. The channel cannot register any of it.

2026-07-30.scoreTotal: CRISIS band — a twelfth session at 25, and the clearest scale-cap edition of the war. Every geopolitical input deteriorated and the score could not move, because both event channels have been maxed since 9–10 Jul. Meanwhile two market lines that were disarmed yesterday are armed today on intraday prints: US-inflation is 3.11 bp through its trigger and Stage-4 Threshold B satisfies both legs for the first time in the war. The two-close rule, not the situation, is what is holding 25.

whatsChanged.title: 4 · What's changed since the last edition (29 Jul → 30 Jul AM)
items: Score holds at 25/30 for a twelfth session. No channel moved. But the strike pause ended, mediation collapsed, the FOMC held against three hike dissents, and two market lines armed intraday. Source: Bloomberg unless stated.

The strike pause is over, and the coalition widened. After four quiet nights (25–28 Jul), the longest of the war, CENTCOM resumed strikes on Iranian territory on the night of 29–30 Jul, ‘a powerful response to yesterday’s attempted Iranian attacks on US forces based in the Middle East.’ The trigger was an intercepted IRGC ballistic-missile salvo at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan and a CENTCOM facility; the first answer was joint US–Saudi strikes on Iran-backed militias across eastern Iraq (at least 20 killed), Riyadh’s first offensive combat action of the war. Quiet-night count back to zero. Source: CENTCOM / Jordan News Agency / Bloomberg / CNBC / CBS News / AP-NPR / Gulf News.

Iran rejected Oman’s Hormuz framework outright. Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi, on state television on 29 Jul: ‘If the route we have proposed is not accepted, no other formula will be accepted. The strait will remain closed, and we are prepared for a restart of war.’ Iran disavowed the internationally established Traffic Separation Scheme, demanded the entire inbound lane under its own control, and reportedly sought ~$1m per ship. Oman is weighing a three-route alternative. No US response to the rejection itself could be found. Source: Reuters / WSJ / Al Jazeera / Middle East Eye.

The FOMC held at 3.50–3.75% on a 9–3 vote, with three dissents for a hike. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all voted for 25 bp. The statement said activity is ‘expanding at a solid pace despite elevated uncertainty that owes, in part, to the conflict in the Middle East’ and that inflation remains above target ‘due in part to the situation in the Middle East causing energy prices to rise.’ Chair Warsh, who has removed forward guidance: ‘There is only a target, and it is 2 percent’; ‘where necessary and appropriate, we will not hesitate to act.’ September hike odds moved to roughly 56% from 32–38%. Source: Federal Reserve press conference transcript / Fox Business / Kiplinger / CNN.

The 30Y printed above 5.20% for the first time on record, arming Stage-4 Threshold B on both legs. The 30Y is 5.2060% intraday (+10.91 bp), 0.60 bp through its Stage-4 leg; the 10Y is 4.6794% (+6.50 bp), 2.94 bp through its own, undoing the reset produced by two sub-4.65% closes. 2s10s steepened 8.97 bp to +40.67 bp, the largest one-day steepening of the war. Intraday only — B needs confirmed closes. The same move killed the Treasury downgrade: the 30Y’s cushion above its 5.00% leg widened from 8.86 bp on Tuesday’s close to 20.60 bp, and MOVE has not printed since 28 Jul (76.09), so its 75 leg is unresolved rather than near release. Source: Bloomberg.

5Y5Y forward inflation broke 2.30% to a war high. 2.3311% (+6.84 bp d/d, +13.16 bp w/w from 2.1995% on 23 Jul), 3.11 bp through the US-inflation upgrade trigger and only the second reading above 2.30% on record after 7 May. The 10Y breakeven rose 7.52 bp to 2.2708%, back above its pre-war anchor after three closes below. One confirmed close starts the clock; a second takes the channel to 5 and the score to 26. Source: Bloomberg.

A new front: gas carriers hit at Damietta, Egypt. Drones struck the Gaslog Salem (Bermuda flag) and the Energos Winter (Marshall Islands, US-owned and operated) at Egypt’s Mediterranean port of Damietta on 29 Jul; fires on both, no casualties, attribution unconfirmed. First strike of the war on the Mediterranean end of the LNG chain. Source: Maritime Executive / Reuters-Ambrey / UKMTO.

The extract’s 29 Jul row never refreshed. Every 29 Jul field is identical to my 29 Jul AM snapshot to four decimal places and MOVE, VIX and SOFR are blank, so there is no 29 Jul close in the data and no reconciliation gap to report. Third-party reporting puts the true 29 Jul close at 2Y 4.33% and 10Y 4.647%, above the stale row. The last fully confirmed close is 28 Jul and every trigger test in this edition runs off it. Source: Bloomberg extract / Kiplinger.

scenarios.name: Return to full war
scenarios.desc: Sharply higher and now the strongest reading of the war. The pause is over, CENTCOM is back over Iran, Saudi Arabia is flying offensive missions, Iran has said it is ‘prepared for a restart of war,’ and the mediation track that restrained all of this for five days no longer exists.
scenarios.path: Brent $105–140; MOVE above 90; oil to 3–4, political to 5, US-inflation to 5; score 28–30.

scenarios.name: Deal collapse — talks stall on terms
scenarios.desc: Raised again. Iran did not stall on Oman’s plan, it rejected it and disavowed the Traffic Separation Scheme underlying any lane arrangement. Oman’s three-route alternative keeps a thread alive, but the gap is now over sovereignty, not sequencing.
scenarios.path: Brent $92–108; oil to 3; 30Y sustained above 5.20% with the 10Y above 4.65%, i.e. Stage-4 B confirmed; score 26–27.

scenarios.name: Contained but violent — blockaded stalemate
scenarios.desc: Lower. This scenario required strikes to stay paused at low intensity; they have resumed, and Saudi entry raises the floor on intensity. It survives only if the resumption is a single retaliatory cycle rather than a new campaign.
scenarios.path: Brent $82–92; MOVE 72–82; risk premium $10–20/bbl; score holds 24–25.

scenarios.name: Regional relapse — Gulf energy infrastructure hit
scenarios.desc: Slightly higher. The Red Sea front reactivated (NCC GHAZAL hit 28 Jul, further Saudi and Bab al-Mandeb attacks 29 Jul), Jizan is still shut, Abqaiq may have taken damage on 27–28 Jul, and Damietta shows reach onto the Mediterranean. A landed hit on the Saudi export corridor is the tail that reprices everything.
scenarios.path: Brent $150+; emergency policy response; HY spreads above 500 bp; score 29–30.

scenarios.name: Mediated pause — the ceasefire sticks
scenarios.desc: Collapsed from 23%. Twenty-four hours ago this was within a point of modal on four quiet nights and a tabled Omani framework. Iran rejected the framework, fired at a US base and drew a resumption; the pause it described no longer exists.
scenarios.path: Brent $74–85; MOVE under 72; Treasury→4, US-inflation→3, escalation→4; score falls toward 19–21.

2026-07-30.scenarioShift: Probability shifts from the 29 Jul edition: mediated pause –15 (23→8) — the single largest one-day move in this map since the war began, and it is a collapse, not a drift; full war +12 (26→38), the highest reading of the war, on the resumption plus Iran’s own ‘prepared for a restart of war’; deal collapse +4 (20→24) on an outright rejection rather than a stall; regional relapse +1 (13→14) on the reactivated Red Sea front and Damietta; contained-but-violent –2 (18→16) because its precondition, a holding pause, is gone. Driver: the de-escalation track that dominated the past week was dismantled in a single 24-hour cycle.
watchlist: US-inflation →5 — the trigger is already through; it needs closes. 5Y5Y prints 2.3311%, 3.11 bp above the 2.30% line and a war high. One confirmed close above 2.30% starts the clock and a second consecutive close takes the channel to 5/5 and the score to 26. This is now the nearest score move and it is an upgrade. Watch whether the post-FOMC breakeven bid holds through a full US session.

Stage-4 Threshold B — both legs armed for the first time in the war. 30Y 5.2060% (0.60 bp through) and 10Y 4.6794% (2.94 bp through), on intraday prints. A confirmed close on both, then persistence, is the most consequential single development available this week. The August refunding cycle is the next coupon-supply test and it now meets a curve that has repriced 11 bp in a session.

MOVE — the missing number. No print since 76.09 on 28 Jul, so there is no post-FOMC rates-vol reading. It matters twice: it is the second leg of the Treasury downgrade test (moot for now) and it is Threshold C. Verify it fresh in the next extract rather than inferring it.

Whether the resumption is one cycle or a new campaign — and whether Oman’s three-route alternative gets any Iranian engagement. Four quiet nights ended with a single retaliatory night. A second and third consecutive night of strikes on Iranian territory converts this from a retaliation cycle into a restarted campaign and would put full war well above 38%; a return to quiet inside 48 hours partially restores the contained-but-violent path. On the diplomatic leg, Gharibabadi’s ‘no other formula will be accepted’ closes the door rhetorically, but Al Jazeera’s sources reported some Iranian flexibility on routing before the rejection — any re-engagement is the only path back toward the mediated-pause branch, now at 8%.

Oil’s failure to price the escalation. Brent added under $3 on a day that produced a strike resumption, Saudi combat entry and the collapse of mediation. Either the market is discounting the resumption as a one-off, or OPEC+ supply and IEA stocks are absorbing more risk premium than assumed. The 2 Aug OPEC+ meeting (a further ~188k b/d expected, then a pause after September) is the test.

Political →5 — stalled at the line, and the cross-read now argues against it. AUTMUSAG has been blank for three sessions at $4.75; AAA’s published regular-grade average eased 0.8¢ between 28 and 29 Jul. Watch the backfill: a print below $4.75 would take the political channel off its trigger for the first time since 24 Jul.

Gas complex — verify the next JGLA print fresh, and watch the Mediterranean. Asia LNG has had no print for two sessions (last ¥3,418 on 28 Jul) and is never carried forward. TTF is back within €2.95 of its war record. The Damietta strike on two gas carriers, one US-owned, is the first hit on the Mediterranean end of the LNG chain and a new risk vector for both series.

methodology.scale: Six transmission channels (maritime denial, oil, US inflation impulse, Treasury stress, political stress, escalation risk), each 0–5, summed to 0–30. Bands: 0–7 watch · 8–14 stress · 15–21 systemic-risk watch · 22–30 crisis. Market channels move only on a confirmed close through a trigger; escalation-risk and maritime denial are event-based. Hysteresis note: upgrades fire on a sustained break, downgrades only on a sustained reversal past a wider threshold, deliberately, to avoid whipsawing. This edition is the most expensive test of the confirmed-close rule on the upside so far: 5Y5Y is 3.11 bp THROUGH its upgrade trigger on an intraday print and the channel still holds at 4, exactly as it held at 3 on 14 Jul against a 2.2061% close with a 0.6 bp margin before firing on the second consecutive close on 15 Jul. The same rule spared the oil channel a whipsaw through both the $95 approach of 23 Jul and the $12.18 unwind that followed. Stage-4 Threshold B is evaluated the same way, which is why both legs being satisfied this morning arms it rather than triggers it.
methodology.scaleCap: Maritime and escalation have been pinned at 5/5 since 10 and 9 Jul. On 30 Jul the strike pause ended, Iran fired ballistic missiles at a US base in Jordan, Saudi Arabia flew its first offensive missions of the war, CENTCOM returned to Iranian territory, Iran rejected the only reopening framework on the table and declared itself ready for a restart of war, and gas carriers were hit at Damietta. Not one of those inputs can raise the score, because the two channels that would register them are already at maximum. The flat 25 must be read as the scale exhausting its geopolitical range, not as a judgment that conditions are stable. Only the four market channels can move the number now, in either direction.
